model_annotation: Figure 3(a) is a line plot illustrating training loss as a function of training steps for multiple methods, with the goal of showing how the loss evolves over time across methods. The x-axis is labeled “Steps” on a linear scale, spanning from 0 to 140,000, with labeled ticks at regular intervals (0, 20k, 40k, 60k, 80k, 100k, 120k, and 140k). The y-axis is labeled “Loss” on a linear scale, spanning approximately from 2.0 to 3.4, with evenly spaced tick marks (about 0.2 increments). The plot contains multiple colored lines with circular markers connected by solid line segments: a red line (Vanilla) that starts near about 3.3–3.4 loss at step 0 and decreases steadily to around ~2.6 by 140k steps; a green line (SepLLM (n=64)) that begins around ~3.0 and declines to roughly ~2.35–2.4 by 140k; a blue line (SepLLM (n=128)) that starts around ~2.9–3.0 and decreases to about ~2.3–2.35 by 140k; a purple line (SepLLM (n=256)) that starts around ~2.8–2.9 and drops to roughly ~2.25–2.3 by 140k; and an orange line (StrmLLM (n=280)) that begins around ~2.85–2.9 and decreases to approximately ~2.25–2.3 by the end, with all non-red methods showing a generally decreasing trend with small step-to-step fluctuations as steps increase.
